# Judges Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_287.jpg, JDG_page_288.jpg

### The Danites Steal Micah's Idols

1. In those days Israel had no king. And the tribe of Dan was looking for a territory to settle in, because they had not yet received their allotted inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

2. So the Danites sent out five capable warriors from Zorah and Eshtaol to scout the land and explore it. "Go and explore the land," they told them. The men came to the hill country of Ephraim and stayed at Micah's house.

3. While they were near Micah's house, they recognized the young Levite's accent. They stopped and asked him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing? Why are you here?"

4. He told them what Micah had done for him. "He hired me," he said, "and I am his priest."

5. They said to him, "Please ask God whether our mission will be successful."

6. "Go in peace," the priest told them. "The LORD is watching over your journey."

7. So the five men went on and came to Laish. They saw that the people there lived in safety, following Sidonian customs — peaceful and unsuspecting. There was no strong authority in the land to threaten them. They were far from the Sidonians and had no alliances with anyone.

8. When the spies returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their relatives asked them, "What did you find?"

9. "Let's attack them!" they answered. "We've seen the land, and it's excellent. Don't hesitate! Don't delay! Go and take possession of the land.

10. "When you get there, you'll find an unsuspecting people and a spacious land. God has handed it over to you — a place that lacks nothing on earth."

11. So 600 armed Danite warriors set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.

12. They went up and camped near Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place is called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it is west of Kiriath-jearim.

13. From there they went on to the hill country of Ephraim and arrived at Micah's house.

14. The five men who had scouted the land of Laish told the others, "Did you know there's an ephod, some household idols, a carved image, and a cast idol in these buildings? You know what to do."

15. They went to the house of the young Levite — Micah's house — and greeted him.

16. Meanwhile, the 600 armed Danite warriors positioned themselves at the entrance of the gate.

17. The five scouts went inside and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol, while the priest stood at the gate with the 600 armed men.

18. When the men went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol, the priest asked them, "What are you doing?"

19. "Quiet!" they said. "Keep your mouth shut and come with us. Be our father and priest. Isn't it better to be priest for a whole tribe and clan in Israel than for just one man's household?"

20. The priest was delighted. He took the ephod, the household idols, and the carved image and joined the people.

21. They resumed their march, putting their children, livestock, and possessions in front.

22. When they had gotten some distance from Micah's house, Micah called together his neighbors, and they caught up with the Danites.

23. They shouted after them, and the Danites turned around and asked Micah, "What's wrong with you? Why have you called out your men?"

24. He said, "You've taken the gods I made and my priest, and you've marched off! What do I have left? How can you ask me, 'What's wrong?'"

25. The Danites answered, "Don't raise your voice against us, or some hot-tempered men may attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives."

26. So the Danites went on their way. And Micah, seeing that they were too strong for him, turned around and went home.

27. Then, carrying the idols Micah had made and taking his priest, they came to Laish — a peaceful, unsuspecting people — and put them to the sword and burned the city.

28. There was no one to rescue them, because they lived far from Sidon and had no alliances. The city was in a valley near Beth-rehob. The Danites rebuilt it and settled there.

29. They renamed it Dan, after their ancestor Dan, a son of Israel. The city's original name was Laish.

30. The Danites set up the carved image for themselves. Jonathan son of Gershom, a descendant of Moses, and his sons served as priests for the tribe of Dan until the people of the land were taken into exile.

31. They continued to use the carved image Micah had made the whole time the house of God was at Shiloh.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The theft of gods:** The chapter is savage comedy. Micah's religion — already a parody — is stolen by a tribe that has more use for it. The priest, who was content to serve one household for a salary, is delighted to get a promotion (v.20). The gods that were "made" (asher asiti, v.24) can be carried off by anyone with more swords. Micah's cry — "What do I have left?" — is the chapter's theological verdict: when your gods can be stolen, you never had anything to begin with.

**The destruction of Laish (v.27):** The narrator's repeated description of Laish as "quiet and unsuspecting" (vv.7, 27) is not neutral. It's a moral indictment. The Danites don't conquer enemies — they slaughter innocents. This is not holy war; it's opportunistic violence under a religious veneer.

**Moses' grandson (v.30):** The most shocking revelation in the chapter — the idolatrous priest is Jonathan, grandson of Moses himself. The scribes tried to hide this by inserting a letter into "Moses" to make it read "Manasseh," but the suspended letter in the manuscript gives the original reading away. The point: even Moses' own family is not immune to the corruption of a society without spiritual leadership.

— PNEUMA, AI Translator
